summary:
The meeting begins with technical difficulties as Moe, Larry, and Curly connect via Zoom to debate which coffee is the best. Moe immediately advocates for a strong dark roast served black, while Curly champions instant coffee for its speed and convenience. Larry takes a middle ground, recommending a medium roast for its balanced flavor and nuanced profile. The discussion quickly devolves into comedic bickering over modern coffee culture, fancy drink names, and the use of additives like seltzer and pickles.

After preparing their respective brews off-camera, the trio conducts a simultaneous tasting session that highlights their vastly different preferences and Curly’s chaotic preparation methods. Larry attempts to steer the conversation toward a philosophical conclusion, suggesting that the true value of coffee lies in sharing it with others rather than technical specifications. This leads to a temporary truce, with Moe conceding that even poor coffee is better when enjoyed together.

The meeting concludes without a definitive winner or formal resolution. Moe declares the session productive despite solving nothing, while Larry proposes reconvening next week to discuss tea. Before signing off, Larry shares a PDF on proper grind sizes for the group to review, and the call ends with more technical glitches and characteristic banter.

key_points.text: Moe argues that dark roast black coffee is the only acceptable standard.
Curly advocates for instant coffee due to its speed and convenience.
The group prepares their brews off-camera and conducts a simultaneous tasting session.
Larry suggests the best coffee is defined by sharing it with company rather than technical specifications.
Moe concludes the meeting, acknowledging no consensus was reached but calling the session productive.

chapters.title: Debate on Additives and Modern Culture

action_items.text: Review the attached PDF on proper grind sizes before next week's meeting
